items.title: NBA Generated $14.5 Billion In Revenue Last Season, Led By Warriors' $895M
items.summary: The NBA generated approximately $14.5 billion in revenue during the 2025-26 season. The 30 teams brought in a combined $13.7 billion, an average of $456 million each, with the rest kept at the league level. The Golden State Warriors led all teams with $895 million in revenue. The Memphis Grizzlies ranked last at $339 million. The totals are after revenue sharing, which moved about $400 million to lower-revenue teams. The NBA's 11-year, $76 billion media deal raised each team's national TV payout from $103 million to $144 million last season. Those payments will rise by approximately seven percent a year on average. Central league revenue made up 41 percent of team revenue. Seating and luxury suites brought in an estimated $3.64 billion. The Warriors led the league with nearly $5.5 million in ticket revenue per game, and the Los Angeles Lakers and New York Knicks each topped $4 million. The Knicks' playoff run generated $180 million in gross revenue. Sponsorships totaled $1.9 billion. Golden State's sponsorship revenue was about $190 million and should top $200 million this season with a new jersey patch deal worth more than $50 million a year. Local media revenue is expected to drop this season after Main Street Sports' bankruptcy affected 13 teams. The Lakers have the NBA's biggest local TV deal, worth about $200 million a year with Spectrum. The average NBA franchise is now worth $6.64 billion, up 21 percent from last year. If Las Vegas and Seattle both join the league, each existing owner would receive more than $500 million in expansion fees, which are not shared with players. The league has said it will decide on expansion by the end of the calendar year.

items.title: LeBron James Shifts To Center As 76ers Beat Knicks In Season Opener
items.summary: LeBron James played center for part of the Philadelphia 76ers' 106-100 season-opening win over the New York Knicks on Tuesday. Joel Embiid said it was his idea after he picked up his third foul late in the second quarter. "I suggested that to the guys, the coaching staff, because I just felt like the way they were calling fouls, I just felt like -- and I was just being honest -- I wasn't going to be as aggressive as I should be on defense, having three fouls, wanting to stay on the floor," said Embiid. "I just told them I thought we should do that." The Sixers trailed 51-46 when Embiid sat down with 2:13 left in the half. James guarded Karl-Anthony Towns the rest of the quarter, and Philadelphia was down just 58-54 at halftime. Nick Nurse said the staff had considered the matchup before the game. Dean Wade is out with a left ankle injury, and backup center Ariel Hukporti is out for the season after Achilles surgery. With the Sixers leading 102-98 in the final two minutes, James denied Towns the ball beyond the arc. OG Anunoby threw crosscourt instead, and Tyrese Maxey intercepted the pass for a dunk that made it a six-point game. "Obviously, KAT is very dangerous when he has space," said James. "I wanted to be there on the catch and not give him no airspace. ... And Tyrese just playing center field was able to jump that and get that dunk. That was a big momentum play." James had 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists to open his record 24th season. Embiid finished with 13 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and three blocks. Embiid compared the plan to Team USA's approach at the 2024 Paris Olympics. In the semifinals against Serbia, James guarded Nikola Jokic.

One of five veterans in camp with the Knicks on a non-guaranteed Exhibit 9 contract, Brown survived the first round of cuts on […]

items.title: Knicks Sign, Waive Dink Pate
items.summary: The Knicks signed free agent wing Dink Pate to an Exhibit 10 contract and subsequently waived him, the team announced today (Twitter links).
